sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r7/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 42 (#41 binary_and_likert_fit_the_ask) and Internal Quality Checks row 42 incl. Mukesh annotation ('we use binary and weighted. Likert we dont use in rewardkit')
evidence: Judged against the shipped format per SKILL.md:65 / quality-checks.md:170 (the workbook internal note that RewardKit practice is binary+weights is the documented known false positive). Gates: render.authenticated_render and constraints.server_backed_local_application are binary (judge.toml:23 each) - pass/fail gate behaviours. Functional: all 16 criteria type=binary (judge.toml lines 43..270) with weights 1.5-4.0; every description is an observable pass/fail behaviour with explicit 'Fails if' conditions (wall refusal, replay refusal, timer deletion, hold scope, stale edit refusal, idempotent send, order, persistence) - none grades degree of craft. Polish: all 6 binary (enter_sends, escape_closes, delete_confirm, link_highlight, transcript_print [scrollWidth==viewport], refusal_in_place) - each is a discrete interaction outcome with a Fails-if clause, matching the template's binary polish shape (template polish judge.toml:20-52). Visual: all 4 craft criteria are type=likert, points=5 (matter_sidebar, retention_marks, transcript_page, phone_chambers; judge.toml:23-73), each with a described anchor at every level 5,4,3,2,1,0; no visual criterion is binary and no likert block lacks anchors. The 0-5 anchor set with points=5 and the prompt's 'Explicit 0-5 scale' section are byte-identical to the frozen template visual prompt (diff of the scale/independence section returned no differences), so that convention is template-controlled, not a task defect. Adversarial: a visually crude app that passes binary transcript_print/link_highlight still loses gradation via likert transcript_page/retention_marks; a conforming app with the matter list on its own screen or no unread counts is explicitly protected in matter_sidebar's preamble; the timer 'notice' in retention_marks matches the brief (walls-and-retention.md:23 'the thread shows the current setting beside the matter title'). Scope: static type/anchor fit only; no configured judge run of visual exists (raw-evidence-index scope), which bears on discrimination rows (40/42), not on this row's format fit.
